scope: HAILSTONE-equivalent first daylight period after the initial fighter sweep, including lagoon shipping, escape traffic, US/Japanese submarines, surface-force geometry and the night-counterstrike gate.

Truk_fast_decks.note: Princeton and Langley are centered on the Eniwetok/CATCHPOLE support split with CVEs; Cabot is campaign-out.

US_force_allocation_center.fast_surface_cover: Most fast battleship/cruiser screen remains with the carriers. A historical full Iowa/New Jersey leaker-hunt is not automatically detached without a worthwhile surface target.

already_evacuated: first-line carriers and major fleet combatants
Hiryu after emergency Truk repair when ferry/recovery-safe
major fleet oilers and high-value tenders

last_convoy.route: west/southwest toward Palau/western Carolines, with route variation rather than a radio-announced fixed convoy lane
last_convoy.purpose: remove seaworthy but lower-priority hulls once 'next dawn' warning becomes HIGH

US_submarine_exit_pickets.logic: US submarines can be positioned on likely Truk exits by the HAILSTONE operation plan even without Branch-forbidden plaintext intelligence; Japanese COMSEC removes exact convoy cueing, not geographic exit interdiction.

last_convoy_centered_contact.result: One western picket obtains a night/periscope-radar contact on the last convoy.
last_convoy_centered_contact.weapon_result: One medium merchant/auxiliary ship of about 4,000-7,000 GRT sunk or constructive-total-loss centered; a second hit is sensitivity only.
last_convoy_centered_contact.Japanese_response: Escort counterattack forces the submarine deep; US submarine survives centered.
last_convoy_centered_contact.high_value_guard: No Akashi/fleet-oiler/carrier is retroactively placed in this convoy.

daylight_air_campaign_after_first_sweep.US_operational_choice: Shift a larger-than-historical share of the next waves to deliberate air-defense suppression because the Japanese plot/radar/AA/fighter system remains coherent and lagoon shipping density is lower.
priority: warning radar/communications/plot nodes and AA fire-direction sites

dusk_Japanese_air_state.interpretation: US has practical daylight air superiority by late afternoon, but Japanese night/recon/harassment capability is not erased.

Truk_fixed_system_damage_by_dusk.airfields: All major strips cratered and cycle-limited; at least one strip remains usable for emergency/small-package launches by dusk after repair-party work.
Truk_fixed_system_damage_by_dusk.air_defense_network: Degraded but not decapitated. One precision AA fire-direction channel remains reliable centered; a second is intermittent/local.
Truk_fixed_system_damage_by_dusk.warning_plot_output: roughly 45-60% of dawn effective throughput centered by late afternoon
Truk_fixed_system_damage_by_dusk.fuel_fire: roughly 3,000-6,000 tons burned/contaminated/isolated by end of first daylight period centered
Truk_fixed_system_damage_by_dusk.communications_power: local outages and damaged nodes; low-bandwidth command connectivity survives through redundancy

lagoon_shipping_day1.interpretation: Still a severe local shipping loss, but radically below historical mass destruction because much of the valuable mobile inventory is already outside Truk.

US_surface_sweep.historical_anchor: Historically Spruance detached Iowa/New Jersey/cruisers/destroyers and destroyed Katori/Maikaze/other leakers after air reports.
US_surface_sweep.branch_center: No full historical TG50.9 gun action. Air/sea search does not find a Katori-class valuable escape group close enough to justify pulling the fast battleships away from the harder-fighting carrier screen.
US_surface_sweep.possible_action: Cruiser/destroyer outer sweep or shore bombardment is limited; may finish a small damaged craft but gains no major surface kill centered.
US_surface_sweep.secondary_effect: Keeping the fast battleships with TF58 slightly strengthens evening/night AA and ASW protection.

Japanese_submarines_near_TF58.useful_contact_nodes: 2-4 favorably placed from the warning arc, with other boats committed to Eniwetok/withdrawal.
Japanese_submarines_near_TF58.daylight_center: One boat obtains a coarse carrier-screen contact/bearing after US launch/recovery activity reveals the operating sector, but does not achieve a satisfactory torpedo firing position.
Japanese_submarines_near_TF58.US_ASW_effect: One Japanese boat is mission-damaged/forced outward centered; no submarine sinking centered during daylight.
Japanese_submarines_near_TF58.information_payoff: The contact plus RI/DF and returning-aircraft observations provides a 1-3 hour-old sector cue for the Japanese night-air counterstrike.

Japanese_surface_fleet.reason: Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu and major surface units are already west of Truk; no fresh weapon-quality TF58 track and no positive-EV reason to reverse into five fleet carriers plus fast battleships.
Japanese_surface_fleet.strategic_action: Continue dispersal toward Palau/Philippines/home-area support nodes while Truk absorbs the fixed-base attack.

night_counterstrike_gate.sources: surviving Truk night-capable attack/recon aircraft plus limited nearby reinforcement/staging only if physically date/range valid
night_counterstrike_gate.cue: submarine/RI/DF sector picture, not an exact carrier position
night_counterstrike_gate.US_state: TF58 is more alert than historical because daylight resistance was substantial and fast battleships remain concentrated with the carriers.
night_counterstrike_gate.next_question: Can Japan convert a stale sector cue into a 20-Feb night torpedo contact, and if so is the payoff a carrier/escort hit or only losses against radar CAP/AA?

Catchpole_interlock.effect: The Truk warning/submarine arc and surviving night-air effort are resources not available at Eniwetok. The Japanese cannot simultaneously mass the same submarines and air crews against both operations.
Catchpole_interlock.US_effect: Princeton/Langley plus CVE/old-BB support can continue the Eniwetok operation while the five fleet carriers and three CVLs sustain Truk suppression.

day1_centered_judgment.air: US clear tactical/operational advantage by dusk, obtained at materially higher aircraft cost than historical HAILSTONE.
day1_centered_judgment.sea: Japanese pre-evacuation prevents the historical surface massacre and saves most high-value mobile assets, but transfers risk into submarine-interdicted escape routes and sacrifices fixed Truk infrastructure.
day1_centered_judgment.base: Truk is wounded, not yet neutralized at dusk. The second day remains necessary if the US objective is to make it unusable as a fleet/air intervention base.
day1_centered_judgment.next: Resolve the 20/21-Feb night counterstrike and submarine/ASW interaction, then the second daylight period and final Truk closeout.
